reason: E1 supports the baseline irradiation tolerance of BCC RHEAs but does not address carbide dispersoids, their formation, or their stability. E2 discusses synthesis of high-surface-area refractory carbides for catalysis, which is unrelated to in situ dispersion strengthening in RHEAs. The key premises about carbide formation, strengthening, defect sinking, and stability under service conditions lack specific prior evidence.
premises: RHEAs with BCC structure exhibit good irradiation tolerance due to lattice distortion and chemical complexity
Nanoscale carbide dispersoids can impede dislocation motion and enhance yield strength via dispersion strengthening
Nanoscale carbide dispersoids can act as sinks for irradiation-induced defects, reducing irradiation hardening
Spark plasma sintering with controlled cooling can produce uniformly distributed nanoscale carbide particles in RHEAs
The carbide dispersoids will remain stable and refined under high-temperature aging and irradiation
